items.title: Security threat prompting PM evacuation linked to Chinese dance group
items.description: The prime minister was forced to evacuate the Lodge last night due to a bomb threat linked to performances in Australia by a classical Chinese dance and music group that is banned in China.

items.title: Live: Albanese urges country to 'turn the heat down' following bomb threat
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has called for the heat to be taken out of political debate after a bomb threat on The Lodge. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Congressman booted as Trump swipes at Supreme Court in State of the Union
items.description: US President Donald Trump addresses Congress in the annual State of the Union speech. Follow live.

items.title: Human remains confirmed as abducted Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian
items.description: The arrests come less than 24 hours after police discovered human remains near a golf club in Sydney's north-west.

items.title: Australian jailed for 7 years for 'betraying' the United States
items.description: A judge in Washington DC has sentenced Australian man Peter Williams to 87 months in prison for selling sensitive information to a Russian broker.

items.title: 'Doesn't the case have to fail?': Judge interrupts closing statement in Coles trial
items.description: The judge overseeing a bombshell federal court case has made a stunning intervention as the consumer watchdog makes closing arguments.

items.title: Colin was on 32 medications. A pharmacist home visit changed his life
items.description: Pharmacists are calling for more funding and caps to be removed from a long-running government program that helps patients avoid hospital.

items.title: Inflation slightly hotter than expected, keeping rate hike on table
items.description: Headline inflation was 3.8 per cent in January, which was unchanged from December, but underlying inflation increased slightly. Both numbers were higher than expected.

items.title: IS-linked families will return 'one way or the other', doctor helping them says
items.description: Australian doctor Jamal Rifi has been helping to coordinate a potential repatriation effort from Syria, including by obtaining passports for the families.

items.title: 'ISIS bride' was 14 when she married a terrorist, sister says
items.description: The sister of an Australian woman who married an Islamic State fighter has revealed how her sister was "groomed" into travelling to a war zone in Syria, where she is now stuck.

items.title: LGBTQIA+ teens bashed and filmed in IS-inspired Sydney attacks
items.description: An ABC investigation has obtained distressing videos and victims' accounts of IS sympathisers hunting and bashing gay and bisexual boys on camera in Sydney.

items.title: Struggling Russian army now losing troops faster than it can replace them
items.description: For the first time since its invasion of Ukraine, Russia has lost troops faster than it can replace them. It's one of many grim milestones of a bloody war that has now been going for four years.

items.title: Shark cull and swimming ban to resume after fatal attack in New Caledonia
items.description: New Caledonian authorities ban beach swimming and resume shark culling despite concern from environmental groups, after a wing foiler is killed in an attack.

items.title: Pastry stall sells 650kg of knafeh in first three days of Ramadan
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attended the opening night of the Ramadan night market in Melbourne's Dandenong, which organisers hope will attract at least a million people over the course of the holy month.

items.title: How a football tackle almost ended up with a leg amputation
items.description: A catastrophic footy injury during a Melbourne reserves game changed Connor Rogers's life in an instant. In the aftermath, the support of his local footy club helped him recover and showed him the power of community. WARNING: This article contains graphic imagery.

items.title: How an 'entitled' Perth obstetrician's drunken behaviour ruined lives
items.description: Sought-after obstetrician Rhys Bellinge appeared to have it all — but that changed in an instant when his drunken, high-speed driving killed a young university graduate and left a rideshare driver with permanent injuries.

items.title: 'I just burst into tears': 400yo viola found after a five-year search
items.description: The instrument is believed to be one of the finest tenor violas in existence and the only surviving example of its kind.

items.title: Lizzie McGuire and Revenge of the Nerds star dies at 71
items.description: Robert Carradine — the youngest member of a legendary Hollywood family —  dies, with his loved ones revealing his struggle with bipolar disorder.

items.title: NT government sued over 44yo mother's death in police watch house
items.description: The family of a woman who died in police custody in Tennant Creek is suing the Northern Territory government for negligence, alleging officers failed in their duty of care after her arrest and that the 44-year-old was held in an "overheated" cell.

items.title: Antisemitism royal commission facing 'limitations'
items.description: The antisemitism royal commission is underway, but it faces some real tests in delivering justice to those impacted in the wake of the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: Mexico president says 'no risk' to FIFA World Cup games despite cartel clashes
items.description: Claudia Sheinbaum says there is "no risk" to fans coming to the country to attend FIFA World Cup games despite the recent capture and death of Mexico's most-wanted cartel leader.

items.title: Could one surgeon undo decades of advocacy for endometriosis?
items.description: Endometriosis sufferers have been left "sick" and reeling over the findings of a months-long ABC investigation into a Melbourne gynaecologist.

items.title: Police with long-arm rifles to patrol Sydney suburbs '24/7'
items.description: More than 200 police officers equipped with long-arm rifles will be deployed to places of worship, major events and mass gatherings like protests on a risk basis.

items.title: Wittenoom traditional owners launch $1.5 billion compensation claim
items.description: Banjima traditional owners say the thousands of hectares left poisoned by decades of asbestos mining have caused one of the highest death rates of mesothelioma in the world.

items.title: Gold Coast Trump Tower developer was 'uncontactable' after business collapse
items.description: The businessman behind a proposed Trump Tower on the Gold Coast ran a development business that collapsed owing $28 million.
